title: Inference mode chooser
description: Answer four questions about a workload to pick real-time, serverless, asynchronous or batch inference, then place ten Cairnway workloads.
intro: Once a model is trained, you still choose how it answers. Set the four questions in the chooser and watch the recommendation change, then place each Cairnway workload and check your choice.
takeaways: Real-time: an always-on endpoint for interactive, low-latency answers, such as a fraud check during checkout.
Serverless: no servers to manage and capacity on demand, for traffic with long idle gaps when a short cold start is acceptable.
Asynchronous: requests are queued and processed when ready, for large payloads (AWS says up to 1 GB) or long processing (up to one hour) when the caller doesn't wait on the line.
Batch (batch transform): predictions for a whole data set in one job, with no persistent endpoint, such as scoring every product overnight.
Serverless is not the same as batch: serverless still answers one request at a time, just without an always-on endpoint.

modes.name: Real-time
modes.summary: An always-on endpoint answers each request in milliseconds to seconds.

modes.name: Serverless
modes.summary: No servers to choose or manage; capacity is provided when requests arrive.
modes.clue: Idle periods, can tolerate a cold start

modes.name: Asynchronous
modes.summary: Requests go into a queue and the result is delivered when it is ready.
modes.clue: Large payloads or long processing, no need to wait on the line

modes.name: Batch
modes.summary: A batch transform job scores a whole data set, writes the results to storage and stops.
modes.clue: Whole data set, scheduled, no persistent endpoint

workloads.text: Check every payment for fraud during checkout, before the order is confirmed.
workloads.why: The customer is waiting, so the answer must come back within a second, and orders arrive all day.

workloads.text: Score demand for all 12,000 products every night for the planning team's morning report.
workloads.why: A whole data set on a schedule, with nobody waiting and no need to keep an endpoint running.

workloads.text: Process large scanned supplier catalogs that take several minutes each; the uploader gets a notification when it is done.
workloads.why: Each request is large and slow, and the caller doesn't wait on the line, so a queue fits.

workloads.text: Check photos of returned items for damage. It is used a few times a day, and a short wake-up delay is fine.
workloads.why: Long idle gaps and a tolerable cold start: no point paying for an endpoint that sits idle.

workloads.text: Show "you may also like" products on every product page as it loads.
workloads.why: Shoppers are waiting for the page, and traffic is steady through the day.

workloads.text: Once a month, score the whole customer list for the chance that each customer stops buying.
workloads.why: A full data set on a schedule; the results go to a file the marketing team reads later.

workloads.text: Analyse long video reviews uploaded by gear testers; each file is several hundred megabytes and takes many minutes to process.
workloads.why: Large payloads and long processing, with the result delivered when ready.

workloads.text: An internal tool that store staff open a few times a week to predict the right boot size for a customer standing in front of them.
workloads.why: An answer is needed on the spot, but traffic is rare, and a second of wake-up time is acceptable.

workloads.text: Re-tag the full 30,000-item catalog with the new category scheme before next month's site redesign.
workloads.why: One pass over a whole data set, with no one waiting on any single item.

workloads.text: Rank results for every search a shopper types on the website.
workloads.why: Interactive and low latency: shoppers expect results as soon as they press Enter, all day long.
